strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 9 datasets and 3 distinct tasks (object classification, action recognition, human pose estimation) with consistently strong results, particularly impressive gains on action recognition (UCF101-DVS: 91.6% vs. previous 78.7%)

Thoughtful Event Cloud representation design that explicitly preserves 2S-1T-1P dimensions, respecting the distinct nature of event data and avoiding the suboptimal treatment of time as a quasi-spatial dimension

Solid ablation studies (Tables 7-8) validating key components; Table 8 particularly informative showing how method scales with event numbers, demonstrating advantage over Point Cloud methods without LSTM for temporal modeling
Clear presentation with reproducible experimental setup including Algorithm 1 pseudocode, detailed hardware specifications, and comprehensive hyperparameter documentation
weaknesses: Incremental novelty: individual components are relatively simple modifications of existing techniques (D-FPS merely scales FPS by factor α; EF-KNN is standard KNN on features; CES is trivial mean operation; Spatial/Temporal-FA apply existing Fourier transform techniques). Experimental comparison fairness issues: FECNet uses 8192-10240 input points vs. TTPOINT/SpikePoint with 1024 points (Tables 1, 4), confounding whether improvements stem from the method or additional input data. Fair comparison would require identical input sizes across all methods

Weak theoretical justification for frequency-domain analysis: claims about temporal convolution ≡ Hadamard product don't directly apply to Spatial-FA (applied to feature dimension, not temporal convolution); why frequency domain specifically helps events lacks theoretical or empirical evidence; no frequency spectrum visualization analysis

Critical design choices lack justification and ablation: scaling factor α in D-FPS appears important but unexplained (learned or fixed? sensitive analysis missing); soft attention mechanism (Eqs. 13-14) mentioned without ablation; feature dimension progression (64→132→268→540) follows 2x+4 rule without justification

Dataset-specific parameter tuning (Table 1: point numbers 1024-10240, sliding windows 30-1500ms) suggests potential overfitting; no cross-dataset robustness analysis or generalization study. Statistical rigor lacking: no error bars, confidence intervals, or multi-run statistics

Missing reproducibility details: code link blank; batch size 'dynamically set' without specifics; unclear whether α is learned or fixed; learnable filter V initialization not specified. Limited discussion of method limitations, failure cases, or when Event Cloud underperforms

Overstated claims: 'frequency-aware' in title suggests sophisticated frequency analysis but applies only standard Fourier + learnable filters; criticism that Point Cloud 'ignores polarity' is unfair (implementation choice, not fundamental limitation); comparison not entirely controlled

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 10 datasets and 3 tasks with extensive ablation studies showing all components contribute meaningfully
Practical value demonstrated through significant preprocessing time improvements (1.5ms vs 14.6ms for Voxel Grid, Table 4) and hardware efficiency (16-64× fewer FPGA cycles)
Well-motivated approach addressing genuine limitations of prior representations with clear positioning relative to voxel and point cloud methods
Solid technical execution with coherent architecture design and proper mathematical formulation; strong engineering throughout

weaknesses: Individual technical components show limited novelty: D-FPS is just learnable coordinate scaling before standard FPS, EF-KNN replaces distance metric, CES is simple mean operation; frequency-aware modules adapt existing FFC/GFNet techniques without fundamental innovation

Thorough ablation studies validating individual components; supplementary analysis in appendices
weaknesses: Limited core technical novelty: Frequency-domain analysis via Fourier transforms not new (FFC 2020, GFNet 2021); application to event clouds is straightforward extension rather than fundamental innovation

Well-motivated architectural innovations combining structural-level polarity integration, learnable D-FPS, feature-based EF-KNN, and frequency-domain analysis specifically tailored to event data properties
